paragraphs.notes: Continuation page inside the claims. Claim 4 ("Benzoylcyclohexandione nach einem der Ansprueche 1 bis 3, worin") opens on the preceding page p95 = printed 93, and this list is the tail of its definition of "R2, R3, R4 und R5 unabhaengig voneinander ...": p95 ends with "Alkylsulfonylamino," and this page opens with "Cycloalkylsulfonylamino,", so the enumeration is unbroken across the page turn. The governing symbol is not reprinted here, so marker is null; the patent carries no [00NN] paragraph markers anywhere. Transcription joins the 23 printed lines into flowing text; three lines end with a word-internal hyphen and the halves are joined without a space: "Heteroaryl-sulfonyl-N-" + "alkyl-amino", "N-Alkyl-N-" + "heteroarylaminocarbonyl", "Alkylcarbonyl-" + "N-arylamino". Nothing here is German prose apart from the connective "oder"; every other token is a chemical group name, so en differs from zh only in lower-casing the names, translating "oder" as "or", and rendering German "Alkinyl" as "alkynyl" and "Halogenalkyl" as "haloalkyl", the convention already used elsewhere in this run. Printed as-is and not corrected: "Heteroaryl-sulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino" carries a hyphen after "Heteroaryl" that its neighbours in the same series do not; "N-Alkyl-N-arylaminocarbonyl-amino" and "Mono- oder Dialkylcarbonylamino" / "Mono- oder Diarylcarbonylamino" are likewise printed with the hyphenation and wording shown.
